en.title: Thief: Dark Project Remastered Trailer Drops Radial Menu, Controller Support
en.summary: Nightdive Studios has unveiled a new trailer for the highly anticipated Thief: The Dark Project Remastered. The gameplay showcase highlights refined mechanics and a new radial menu for Garrett's tools.
en.body:
The shadows are stirring once more as **Nightdive Studios** has gifted fans a substantial look at **Thief: The Dark Project Remastered** with a new trailer. Unveiled during the PC Gaming Show’s Tokyo Direct showcase, this nearly 90-second glimpse offers more than just updated visuals; it dives deep into the core gameplay loop that made **Thief** a legendary stealth experience.

Players will once again step into the worn boots of **Garrett**, the master thief, tasked with pilfering treasures from heavily guarded locales. The trailer effectively demonstrates how players will navigate intricate levels, utilizing **Garrett's** signature tools to avoid detection and overcome obstacles. From picking locks with precision to using arrows to manipulate light and shadow, the classic stealth mechanics are on full display. A particularly exciting reveal for many will be the emphasis on controller support. To make **Garrett's** vast arsenal more accessible on gamepads, **Thief: The Dark Project Remastered** introduces a slick radial item wheel, allowing for quick selection of lockpicks, specialized arrows, and other essential gadgets without breaking immersion. This thoughtful addition ensures that both keyboard and mouse veterans and controller-wielding players can experience the game’s refined gameplay. The developers have confirmed that the remaster will feature graphical improvements, aiming for a stunning 4K resolution and a smooth 120 FPS, bringing the dark, atmospheric world of **Thief** to life like never before.

## A New Way to Play

The inclusion of enhanced controller support, complete with rumble and gyro functionality, is a significant move for a game that originally defined first-person stealth on PC. This isn't just about making the game playable on consoles; it's about offering *new* ways to interact with the world. The radial menu, in particular, is a game-changer, streamlining the often-frenetic decision-making process that comes with managing **Garrett's** diverse inventory under pressure. Fans have long debated the best way to control **Garrett** on a gamepad, and **Nightdive Studios** appears to have listened, providing a solution that feels both modern and true to the spirit of the original. This focus on accessibility and refined control schemes signals a deep respect for the source material while embracing contemporary gaming expectations.

## What’s Next for the Master Thief

While **Thief: The Dark Project Remastered** was officially announced back in June, a firm release date remains elusive. Players can mark their calendars for a Winter 2026 window, with the game slated to launch across PC, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch. Further details regarding specific features and potential early access opportunities are expected as the release window approaches.

content_raw: Nightdive Studios has released a new trailer for the upcoming Thief: The Dark Project Remastered . The trailer, which you can check out below, clocks in at just over 90 seconds and was unveiled during the PC Gaming Show’s Tokyo Direct showcase. The core premise of the trailer revolves around protagonist Garrett getting a message from a mysterious client hiring him to get something. Rather than strictly focusing on the story, however, the trailer instead showcases the gameplay of Thief: The Dark Project Remastered . The trailer also explains the core gameplay loop of the title, which will have players sneaking into large buildings, avoiding guards by using a variety of tools, and stealing just about anything that isn’t nailed to the ground. Throughout the trailer, we also get a good look at many of the intricate levels that make up the main campaign of Thief: The Dark Project Remastered . One of the most interesting things showcased in the trailer is the controller support that will be added to the remaster. Supporting control schemes aside from keyboard and mouse involves giving players an easier way to access the plethora of tools they will have at their disposal, which Thief: The Dark Project Remastered handles by introducing a radial item wheel through which Garrett can pick between lockpicks, arrows, and other items. The title was officially announced back in June and is slated for release across PC, PS4, PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch, and the Nintendo Switch 2. However, it doesn’t yet have a release date aside from a Winter 2026 window. Controller players are in for some added benefits, however, thanks to the inclusion of rumble and gyro support, giving players an entirely new way to experience the first-person stealth classic. Earlier this month, Nightdive Studios had confirmed that, along with featuring the core campaign from the original release, Thief: The Dark Project Remastered will also include a second campaign, dubbed The Tarnished Mirror . The campaign was teased through a trailer and is essentially a critically acclaimed collection of fan-created levels that come together to tell an entirely new story. Thief: The Dark Project was originally released in 1998 and is considered one of the seminal works of the immersive sim genre alongside titles like Deus Ex and System Shock 2 . Developed by Looking Glass Studios, Thief: The Dark Project follows the story of a young street urchin, Garrett, who was taken in by an organization known as the Keepers. By spending time with this organization, Garrett is able to learn many of the skills that would go on to earn him a reputation of being one of the greatest thieves ever. Along with its importance to the immersive sim genre, Thief: The Dark Project is also considered one of the two titles – alongside Metal Gear Solid – to have essentially defined stealth gameplay, with elements from the title showing up even in modern games.
